Preliminary Results — Walking Intervention vs Control (pre–post)

Data coverage (consistent):
  • Structural (subcortical volumes): FULL cohort — n=53 (29 C / 24 W; sub-057 ses-02 excluded for failed segmentation)
  • Functional connectivity (fc variant): n=43 subjects (88 sessions; 48 with both sessions − 5 FD>0.3mm excluded: 062, 070, 072, 082, 090)
  • Voxelwise (ALFF/ReHo) + seed-to-voxel: OLD cohort — n=38–39 (TFCE rerun on expanded cohort in progress)

1. Methods

1.1 Design & cohort

Longitudinal walking-intervention study: 2 groups (Walking intervention vs Control) × 2 timepoints (pre = ses-01, post = ses-02). Analysis cohort: two-timepoint subjects with usable data. All models estimate the group×time interaction = the intervention effect (differential change between groups over the intervention period).

1.2 Preprocessing

  • fMRIPrep 25.2.5 (MNI152NLin6Asym res-2 output; no recon-all)
  • XCP-D 26.0.2 denoising, fc variant: aCompCor nuisance regression, FD scrubbing (>0.3mm), bandpass 0.01–0.08 Hz, notch filter 12–18 Hz, 6mm smoothing. All confounds (motion, aCompCor, scrubbing) are regressed at this stage — no re-regression downstream.
  • FastSurfer 2.5.4 segmentation (subcortical volumes).

1.3 Functional connectivity estimation

  • ROI timeseries from XCP-D denoised BOLD using the 442-parcel atlas (Schaefer2018 400 + Tian subcortex S2 + 10 cerebellar regions, MNI152NLin6Asym 2mm).
  • Connectivity matrices: Pearson correlation → Fisher-z.
  • Metrics per subject/session: within/between-network mean z (9 blocks), ROI-to-network z, ROI-to-whole-brain z, ROI homogeneity, graph metrics (strength, clustering, efficiency), and 9-block partial correlation.
  • Estimators explained:
    • partial = full 442-node partial correlation (Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage). Conditioning on all 440 other ROIs makes between-block values near-zero, so this estimator is used for ROI-level metrics (roi_to_wholebrain_z, roi_to_network_z) where it is well-conditioned.
    • partial_9block = partial correlation on the 9 network-block mean timeseries (Yeo 7 networks + subcortex + cerebellum). Conditioning on only 9 signals keeps between-network effects interpretable.
    • Why not simple Pearson? The LMM value ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject) fails to converge (singular Hessian) for the Pearson/Spearman versions of these metrics — the random-effects structure is degenerate after FD adjustment. The partial-correlation versions are better conditioned and converge reliably, so they are the reported estimators. Pearson matrices are still used for the raw connectivity matrices and 2×2 plots.

1.4 Statistical models

  • Structural: LMM volume ~ group×time + Age + Gender + ICV + (1|subject); BH-FDR across 10 structures.
  • FC: LMM value ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject); BH-FDR per estimator family.
  • Voxelwise (ALFF/ReHo): per-subject delta maps (ses-02 − ses-01), two-sample t-test (Walking vs Control) via FSL randomise, TFCE, 5000 permutations.
  • Seed-to-voxel: per-subject seed-to-whole-brain Pearson maps (Fisher-z), delta maps, two-sample t-test via FSL randomise TFCE (5000 perms).

2. Executive Summary

Walking intervention preserves subcortical volume and alters motor-system connectivity.
  • Structural (full cohort, n=53): 7 subcortical structures show FDR-significant group×time effects — Walking preserves or gains volume while Control declines (amygdala-R, thalamus L/R, putamen L/R, hippocampus L/R; q=.026–.032).
  • Functional connectivity (n=43): the most robust effect is reduced left motor cortex whole-brain coupling (partial correlation, q=.001) and reduced motor–somatomotor coupling (q=.030) in Walking vs Control.
  • Seed-to-voxel (old cohort): red nucleus seeds → increased connectivity to motor/precentral/SMA; left hippocampal head → right temporal — all Walking > Control (TFCE p<.05).
  • Local measures: convergent ALFF + ReHo group×time cluster in left visual cortex.
  • Caution: FC findings are sensitive to sample composition (see §9.2); motor-cortex findings are the most robust. Voxelwise results are old-cohort only.

3. Structural — subcortical volume preservation (FULL cohort, n=53)

What we did: FastSurfer deep-learning segmentation of T1w; extracted subcortical volumes (mm³) per subject/session; LMM with ICV covariate; BH-FDR across 10 structures. The group×time interaction tests differential change.

7 structures FDR-significant: Walking preserves or gains volume; Control declines — amygdala-R, thalamus L/R, putamen L/R, hippocampus L/R.

5. Voxelwise local measures (old cohort, n=38–39, fc)

What we did: ALFF and ReHo computed voxelwise from XCP-D denoised BOLD; per-subject delta maps; two-sample t-test via FSL randomise TFCE (5000 perms).

Convergent ALFF + ReHo group×time cluster in left visual cortex (MNI −38, −98, −4; Schaefer Vis_12), cluster-corrected p<.05.

6. Seed-to-voxel connectivity (old cohort, n=39, fc, delta + TFCE 5000 perms)

What we did: per-subject seed-to-whole-brain Pearson correlation maps (Fisher-z); per-subject delta maps (ses-02 − ses-01); two-sample t-test (Walking vs Control on deltas) via FSL randomise TFCE (5000 perms). Positive t = Walking's connectivity change > Control's. Seed locations are shown before each result.

3 seeds significant (all Walking > Control change): left/right red nucleus → motor/precentral/SMA; left hippocampal head → right temporal/parahippocampal.

8. Summary forest plot

9. Supplementary analyses

9.1 Outlier analysis

4 extreme values (|z|>4 within group×session) found, all in graph metrics (mean_clustering ×2, mean_strength ×1 from sub-076; roi_to_wholebrain_z ×1 from sub-088). None of the significant findings' metrics contain outliers. sub-076 FD is low (0.13–0.17) — not a motion artifact.

9.2 Sensitivity: excluding sub-076

FC results are sensitive to sub-076:
  • fc: Motor_L–SomMot SURVIVES (t=−2.88, q=.006, stronger); Cont–Vis survives (q=.028); new findings appear (Vis–SalVentAttn, DLPFC_L–Vis, SomMot within, Cont–DorsAttn)
Conclusion: Motor_L whole-brain and Motor_L–SomMot are the most robust; other FC findings are fragile and hypothesis-generating.

9.3 FD threshold sensitivity

At FD>0.5 (only sub-072 excluded, n=48): Motor_L whole-brain survives (q=.004); Motor_L–SomMot drops; Cont–Vis flips sign (unstable). Motor_L whole-brain is robust across thresholds.

9.4 Exclusions

  • sub-057 ses-02: failed FastSurfer segmentation (all subcortical ≈0 mm³) — excluded from structural
  • sub-062, 070, 072, 082, 090: mean FD > 0.3mm — excluded from FC
  • sub-076: graph-metric outlier — sensitivity analysis only

9.5 Null results (did NOT survive)

  • DKT cortical volumes (best q=.30)
  • FIRST (FSL) hippocampal volumes
  • Caudate, left amygdala volumes
  • Delta-TFCE voxelwise contrasts
  • Most graph metrics and edge-wise FC

10. Caveats

  • Preliminary — FDR used, not permutation max-T; no split-half replication
  • FC = fc variant only (n=43); full n=52 pending XCP-D completion
  • Voxelwise + seed-to-voxel = old cohort only (TFCE rerun on expanded cohort in progress)
  • Volumes from FastSurferVINN (deep-learning) segmentation; longitudinal thickness pending
  • FC findings sensitive to single subjects (see §9.2)
  • No EC (effective connectivity) results yet — SPM/DCM pipeline pending
